title: Subarray Sum Equals K
summary: Count contiguous subarrays summing to k. A subarray (j, i] sums to k exactly when `prefix[i] − prefix[j] = k`. Walk once keeping a map of how often each prefix sum has appeared; at each position add the count of `prefix − k`.

complexity.note: One pass with a hash map.

intuition: Subarray sum = difference of two prefix sums.
`seen.get(prefix - k)` = number of earlier start points that work.
Seed the map with `{0: 1}` so subarrays starting at index 0 count.
Works with negative numbers, unlike a sliding window.
pitfalls: Sliding window fails with negative numbers.
Forgetting the `{0: 1}` seed misses subarrays from the start.
Updating the map before checking counts the empty subarray when k = 0.

def subarraySum(nums: List[int], k: int) -> int:
    seen = Counter({0: 1})
    prefix = count = 0
    for x in nums:
        prefix += x
        count += seen[prefix - k]
        seen[prefix] += 1
    return count

title: Next Permutation
summary: Rearrange numbers into the next lexicographically larger permutation, in place. Find the rightmost index i with `nums[i] < nums[i+1]` (the pivot). Swap it with the smallest larger value to its right, then reverse the suffix after i to make it as small as possible.

complexity.note: At most two scans and one reversal.

intuition: The suffix after the pivot is non-increasing: it's already the largest arrangement of those numbers.
To get the next permutation, bump the pivot up by the smallest possible amount.
The suffix stays non-increasing after the swap, so reversing makes it ascending (smallest).
No pivot means the array is the last permutation: reverse it all.
pitfalls: Swapping with the first larger element instead of the rightmost (smallest) larger one.
Sorting the suffix instead of reversing it: correct but O(n log n).
Using `>` instead of `>=` when scanning for the pivot, which breaks with duplicates.

def nextPermutation(nums: List[int]) -> None:
    i = len(nums) - 2
    while i >= 0 and nums[i] >= nums[i + 1]: i -= 1

    nums[i + 1:] = reversed(nums[i + 1:])

def spiralOrder(matrix: List[List[int]]) -> List[int]:
    res = []
    top, bottom, left, right = 0, len(matrix) - 1, 0, len(matrix[0]) - 1
    while top <= bottom and left <= right:
        res += [matrix[top][c] for c in range(left, right + 1)]
        top += 1
        res += [matrix[r][right] for r in range(top, bottom + 1)]
        right -= 1
        if top <= bottom:
            res += [matrix[bottom][c] for c in range(right, left - 1, -1)]
            bottom -= 1
        if left <= right:
            res += [matrix[r][left] for r in range(bottom, top - 1, -1)]
            left += 1
    return res
